A public interest litigation has been filed before the Supreme Court seeking directions to declare the Baiga-dominated Birsa and Baihar blocks of Madhya Pradesh's Balaghat district an epidemic-prone area under the Epidemic Diseases Act, 1897, following deaths of over 30 tribal children due to measles-rubella and severe malnutrition.

A bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V. Mohana today issued notice to the Union, the State, NHRC and other official respondents on the plea after hearing Advocate Varun Thakur for the petitioner.

The petition alleges that administrative negligence, inadequate healthcare facilities, malnutrition and a failure to ensure timely immunisation contributed to the deaths of children in remote tribal settlements.
It seeks compensation for affected families, the provision of safe drinking water and nutritious food, and implementation of government welfare schemes for the tribal community.

“Despite robust statutory frameworks specifically designed to protect their habitat and existence, the State apparatus has manifested a colossal systemic failure, allowing a treatable viral infection to decimate an already fragile population.

Despite explicit, written warnings submitted to the district administration and public representatives as early as January 2026, the State apparatus remained in a bureaucratic slumber”, the plea states.
More than 35 children belonging to the Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Group (PVTG) have reportedly died in the affected areas following an outbreak of measles-rubella and severe malnutrition.
The petition alleges that the administration failed to undertake adequate disease surveillance, provide essential medicines and deploy medical teams despite being alerted to the situation.

The petition also challenges an order issued by the Additional District Magistrate of Balaghat on September 3 under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 prohibiting citizens, journalists and healthcare workers from photographing, recording videos or reels, or publishing information about conditions inside public offices and health facilities on social media.
The petition contends that the restriction is meant to suppress evidence of administrative failures and infringes the constitutional right to freedom of speech and expression.
Notably, the Balaghat administration withdrew the September 3 order within hours of issuing it, stating that it had been issued in haste and was not intended to prevent media coverage.

article_sentences: Senior Advocate Kapil Sibal and other lawyers urged the Court to hear the matter today itself.

A petition has been filed in the Supreme Court challenging the cancellation of the train services to Delhi, the shutdown of metro stations and the internet imposed in the capital ahead of the October 10 protests announced by the CJP against the Chief Election Commissioner.
Senior Advocate Kapil Sibal made an urgent unlisted mentioning before the Chief Justice of India, seeking the hearing of the matter today itself.
"What is happening to my country?" Sibal exclaimed.

He submitted that various trains which are scheduled to arrive in New Delhi and Nizamuddin stations between 4 AM and 2 PM on October 10 have been cancelled, and hotels have been asked to stop taking guests.
Also 57 metro stations spread across Central, South, North, North-West, North-East and East Delhi have been shut from 9 PM today onwards.

When Chief Justice of India Surya Kant asked why the Delhi High Court cannot be approached, Sibal said that there was a similar petition (filed by the Indian Youth Congress) in the Delhi High Court, which was adjourned till Monday.
The bench asked Sibal if he was representing any person who was organising the protest.
Sibal replied that he was representing MA Baby, CPI(M) Secretary, though he was not an organiser of the protest himself.
Justice Joymalya Bagchi then pointed out that he was not an organiser, and had not applied for permission to protest.
If there is no permission to protest, it would be an unlawful protest, Justice Bagchi said.
The Judge added that if the protests are without permission, then the protesters may face the risk of prosecution.

stories.title: Leading dentists redefining modern dentistry through innovation, impact and excellence
stories.summary: Dentistry today extends far beyond traditional clinical care. From advanced implantology and digital orthodontics to cosmetic dentistry, preventive healthcare, and dental education, a new generation of practitioners is reshaping how oral healthcare is delivered and understood.These dentists come from diverse backgrounds and bring different areas of expertise, but they share a common focus on combining clinical knowledge with innovation, patient care, education, and meaningful impact. Their work reflects the evolving face of dentistry, where technology, entrepreneurship, sustainability, and community service are increasingly becoming part of the profession.Dr. Arumalla Sridhar Reddy: Transforming Lives Through Dentistry and Community Service Dr. Arumalla Sridhar Reddy, an Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeon, has made community healthcare a significant part of his professional journey. He has provided free dental health checkups to more than 1.2 million schoolchildren across underserved communities and holds a Guinness World Record for conducting the world’s largest dental health checkup, covering 21,233 students within eight hours.His contributions extend beyond dental care, with Dr. Reddy supporting three orphanage homes that provide care, education, and healthcare to around 250 children.He has also facilitated thousands of free orthognathic surgeries for underprivileged patients and has reportedly received the President of India’s Gold Medal twice for contributions to social service and community welfare.Dr. Shilfa Nigar: Innovating Sustainable DentistryDr. Shilfa Nigar is a practising cosmetic dentist and entrepreneur, building her next chapter around Ecoligners, a dental venture focused on making eco-friendly aligner treatment more accessible and sustainability-conscious. The venture aims to address the waste associated with disposable clear aligners by exploring recyclable solutions and bringing an environmental perspective to modern orthodontic treatment.With nearly a decade of clinical experience, Dr. Shilfa has also been recognised as India’s first General Dental Practitioner to achieve Black Diamond Invisalign Provider status. Beyond dentistry, she has created work-from-home opportunities for around 100 female dentists, enabling them to continue working outside conventional clinical practice.Her journey reflects the intersection of clinical expertise, entrepreneurship, sustainability and social impact.Dr. M. Vijaya Lakshmi Macherla: Crafting Personalised SmilesDr. M. Vijaya Lakshmi Macherla is a dental surgeon, implantologist, and smile designing specialist with 28 years of experience. A first-generation doctor, she began her practice in 2009 with a single dental chair and has since expanded it to three branches in Hyderabad, with a team of doctors and predominantly female staff. Her work in smile designing focuses on creating natural-looking, personalised smiles based on each patient’s facial features, dental needs, and expectations.Beyond clinical practice, Dr. Vijaya Lakshmi has focused on continuous learning with predominantly women-led clinical and support staff. She has also built a social media community of over 3 lakh people, where she shares dental awareness and practical health tips. She has conducted dental camps in government schools and supported free consultations for orphans and physically challenged individuals, along with treatment concessions through social initiatives.Her professional journey also includes advanced training and exposure to international dental programmes, veneers, and digital dentistry, alongside recognition for her contributions to the field.Dr. Prathamesh Kshatriya: Building a New Age Healthcare EcosystemDr. Prathamesh Kshatriya, an oral implantologist and healthcare entrepreneur, has spent nearly eight years studying content, marketing and the psychology behind what makes people pay attention. That experience led him to build Vantage & Cole, a healthcare-focused growth company working with doctors, clinics, hospitals and healthcare brands across positioning, communication, digital growth and market strategy.Kshatriya has also worked behind the scenes as a consultant and growth advisor to healthcare businesses, helping shape how they communicate, position themselves and connect with their audiences. Known for a storytelling style that often gives language to what doctors and students are already thinking or feeling, he has developed a distinctive presence within the healthcare community.Alongside this, he has built Doctors Coach into a community of more than 2 Lakh doctors, dentists and healthcare students, with conversations spanning money, artificial intelligence, entrepreneurship and emerging career opportunities. His work today brings together healthcare, storytelling, media and business.Dr. Prajakta Nawgiri: Transforming Smiles Through Modern DentistryDr. Prajakta Nawgiri is a Cosmetic and Paediatric Dentist and the Founder and Chief Dentist of VISTA Dental, Pune, an award-winning multispeciality dental practice. With over 12 years of experience across Mumbai and Pune, including five years in corporate dentistry, she has treated more than 8,000 patients and built VISTA Dental around clinical excellence, aesthetics and a patient-centric approach.Specialising in cosmetic dentistry and smile designing, Dr. Prajakta focuses on personalised and natural-looking smile transformations. Her practice integrates digital dentistry and advanced dental technology into diagnosis, treatment planning and patient care. Her clientele includes celebrities, entrepreneurs and professionals, with patients travelling from across India and internationally for treatment. A recipient of two FAMDENT Excellence in Dentistry Awards, her journey brings together clinical practice, entrepreneurship and the evolution of a modern, technology-driven dental practice.Dr. Kavita Bhat Kumar: 30 Years of Transforming SmilesDr. Kavita Bhat Kumar is a cosmetic dentist and founder of Designer Smiles, a multispeciality dental clinic in Vile Parle East, Mumbai, which she has led since 1995. With over 30 years of clinical experience, she has built her practice around smile makeovers and aesthetic dentistry, focusing on personalised, natural-looking and conservative treatment. Over the years, her practice has attracted clientele including professionals, models, public figures and patients travelling from overseas for dental care. Her training includes advanced aesthetic dentistry in Germany and specialised education in soft and hard tissue lasers at the University of Bonn.Her approach combines technology with clinical judgement, while giving equal importance to patient comfort and the overall treatment experience. As an Invisalign provider, she incorporates clear aligner therapy into selected cases. Under her leadership, Designer Smiles received the FAMDENT Excellence in Dentistry Award for Clinic of the Year in 2021. She is also a member of the Indian Academy of Aesthetic & Cosmetic Dentistry.Dr. Rachita Guru: Making Dental Education Digital Dr. Rachita Guru is an MDS Orthodontist, Gold Medallist and Invisalign Provider who practises across Gurgaon, Lucknow and Sonipat. She specialises in digital orthodontics, clear aligner therapy and aesthetic smile transformations, while incorporating digital technology into contemporary treatment planning. Her experience as an orthodontic patient during her postgraduate years also shaped her approach to patient education and understanding the questions and concerns people face during treatment.Since starting dental education content during the COVID-19 pandemic, Dr. Rachita has built an organic social media community of more than 31,000 followers, using digital platforms to make dental science simpler and more accessible. She also conducts courses, webinars and personal branding sessions for dentists. Her work in dental education has earned her the National Icon Award from the Indian Dental Association, and she was also nominated for Social Media Dentist of the Year 2026 at the Famdent Awards.Dr. Naresh Kumar: Advancing Implant Dentistry Through Innovation Dr. Naresh Kumar is a Hyderabad-based prosthodontist and implantologist with more than two decades of clinical experience, specialising in advanced implant dentistry, All-on-X rehabilitation, digital dentistry, and zygomatic implant procedures. As the founder of Vivasmilez Dental, he focuses on complex implant and full mouth rehabilitation cases, combining clinical expertise with evolving digital workflows.Beyond patient care, Dr. Kumar has contributed to dental education and professional development, having trained more than 500 dentists in advanced implant dentistry. Through training programmes, lectures and keynote sessions, he has worked to share his experience and expertise with fellow dental professionals, reflecting the growing role of technology and advanced techniques in modern implantology.Dr. Swati Bharti: Redefining Excellence in Cosmetic DentistryDr. Swati Bharti is a Manipal-trained dentist with more than 25 years of experience, with a clinical focus on root canal treatment, aesthetic and cosmetic dentistry. Dr. Bharti remains closely involved throughout the patient journey, from consultation and clinical planning to post-treatment care and follow-up. Her approach combines aesthetic sensitivity, clinical precision and clear communication, helping Rootz Dentz build long-standing relationships with patients across generations while maintaining a highly personalised approach to dental care.Dr. Shweta N. Lokhande: Championing Preventive and Sustainable Dentistry Dr. Shweta N. Lokhande is a dentist, lecturer, author, global health researcher, oral health educator and certified career counsellor whose work brings together clinical practice, education, public health and community impact. With expertise in global health and research, she advocates for preventive, accessible and sustainable healthcare. As teaching faculty in Community Medicine, she contributes to teaching, mentoring, research supervision, curriculum development, scientific publications and professional preceptorship. Her experience as a registered Dental Care Professional in the UK further informs her perspective on equitable, patient-centred care.Beyond academics and research, Dr. Lokhande promotes engaging, eco-conscious oral health education and community well-being. She also heads the Institutional Forum for Women Empowerment (IFFW), where she works to advance women’s education, confidence, leadership and financial independence. stories.headline: Indian-origin South African jurist Navi Pillay wins 2026 Nobel Peace Prize
stories.title: Indian-origin South African jurist Navi Pillay wins 2026 Nobel Peace Prize
stories.summary: Norway, Oct 9 : Indian-origin South African jurist and human rights pioneer Navanethem “Navi” Pillay, former United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights, was awarded the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize on Friday for her efforts to promote peace and international law, the Norwegian Nobel Committee announced. In its official announcement on Friday, the committee said Pillay had demonstrated exceptional courage and integrity in advancing a more comprehensive global legal order and had played a significant role in ensuring that war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide are prosecuted. “The Nobel Peace Prize for 2026 goes to a person who with exceptional courage and integrity has led the way towards a more comprehensive global legal order. This year’s laureate has been instrumental in ensuring that war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide are prosecuted,” the press release stated. In a post on X announcing the award, the Nobel Prize account said, “Today Navi Pillay has been awarded the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize for her efforts to promote peace and international law.” The Nobel Committee highlighted Pillay’s long career in advancing universal legal principles, from her early work defending Nelson Mandela and others who opposed apartheid in South Africa to her service as a judge in major international legal cases. “Born into a family of Indian Tamil origin under apartheid in Durban, South Africa, Pillay became a lawyer and legal pioneer, confronting deep structural discrimination, segregation and exclusion,” the committee said. Pillay has served as a judge on South Africa’s High Court, the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda and the International Criminal Court. She also served as the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights and, until recently, chaired the UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory. She is currently a judge at the International Court of Justice in the case in which Myanmar stands accused of genocide, according to the Nobel Committee. The committee noted that Pillay had helped demonstrate how legal measures could prevent acts of war and violence while strengthening international legal institutions. In a post on X, the Nobel Prize account emphasised the importance of international law in addressing conflicts peacefully. “More and more conflicts are being addressed through diplomacy, treaties and legal mechanisms, rather than threats, violence and warfare. International law is a foundation for a more peaceful world,” the post said. It added, “At a time of existential challenges - including more wars and conflicts than the world has seen in a long time – international law is no longer just a supplement to peace and security. It is an absolute necessity.” The Nobel Committee also highlighted Pillay’s contribution to landmark legal developments in the prosecution of sexual violence and genocide. “When the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda established that rape and sexual violence could constitute a crime against humanity – as well as genocide - her influence was a significant factor,” the committee said. It added that Pillay was instrumental in a separate legal breakthrough in the same case, in which a defendant faced charges of incitement to commit genocide purely based on "spreading propaganda". The committee said Pillay had held states and national leaders accountable while bringing hope to victims of violence and conflict. Throughout her career, she has emphasised the responsibility of individuals and states to comply with the rule of law. The award also comes amid what the committee described as growing pressure on the international legal system and its institutions. “We see a shift towards power politics at the expense of legal frameworks and global respect for law and justice. Whenever might overtakes right, it undermines stability, trust and peaceful co-existence,” the press release stated. Explaining the significance of the award, the committee said, “In awarding this year’s Nobel Peace Prize, the Norwegian Nobel Committee wants to remind the world that the rule of law - national and international - underpins the system we have set up to ensure peace and resolve conflicts non-violently. Peace requires justice.” The committee further said that Pillay’s career demonstrated the importance of protecting and expanding international legal principles. “Navi Pillay’s commitment to justice and human dignity is a source of hope and inspiration to all who seek to bring about a more peaceful world,” it said. The Nobel Committee said the 2026 Peace Prize was rooted in Alfred Nobel’s will, highlighting Pillay’s contribution to strengthening fraternity between nations and advancing the use of tribunals to promote peace and justice.

stories.headline: SC seeks response of States, UTs on plea alleging prolonged vacancies in power regulatory bodies
stories.title: SC seeks response of States, UTs on plea alleging prolonged vacancies in power regulatory bodies
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 9: The Supreme Court on Friday sought a response from 15 states and the Union Territories of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh on a PIL filed by NGO Energy Watchdog seeking directions to ensure that their state electricity regulatory commissions are properly constituted under the law. The bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana issued notice on the PIL filed by the NGO through lawyer Pranav Sachdeva. The petitioner has sought the apex court's directions directing the states and UTs to take all steps to comply with the provisions of the Electricity Act, 2003, and with the directions of the apex court in a verdict of April 2018 regarding composition of State Electricity Regulatory Commissions (SERCs). The plea said there were several "statutory infractions", such as prolonged vacancies in the offices of chairperson and members and the complete absence of a person of law on the Commission, across 230 SERCs in the 15 states and the UTs. In the 2018 ruling, the Supreme Court held that SERCs have the "trappings of the court" and must have a suitably qualified person of law as a member, the plea said. It said the commissions across several states, including West Bengal, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Kerala, Himachal Pradesh, Meghalaya, Manipur, Mizoram and Nagaland, continue to lack a person of law despite this ruling. The plea said in Tamil Nadu, all three offices are vacant, while in Andhra Pradesh, the chairperson and member (technical) posts are vacant, and the Commission functions with a sole member (finance). It said that in West Bengal, only the chairperson's office has been created, and the incumbent does not have the required legal background. The plea said the failure "strikes at consumers' access to justice" under Articles 14 and 21 of the Constitution and, without the mandated person of law, consumers cannot get lawful adjudication of complaints under the Electricity Act. "Consumers' access to that remedy cannot be made dependent upon indefinite executive inaction," the plea said. It sought directions to the states of West Bengal, Madhya Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, Kerala, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, Meghalaya, Manipur, Nagaland, Mizoram and Sikkim, and to the UTs of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh, directing the authorities concerned to file a reply disclosing the steps taken to ensure that their SERCs had been constituted in compliance with the Electricity Act provisions.

Logistics contributed more than 13 per cent to India’s GDP and played a critical role in supporting manufacturing growth.

The two sectors were complementary, making efficient logistics infrastructure essential to strengthening the country’s manufacturing ecosystem, he said while addressing at PRISM 2026 – Powering Recognition: India’s Skill Movement, hosted by the Logistics Sector Skill Council (LSC) in association with National Skill Development Council on Friday.
A study conducted by DPIIT in 2025 estimated India’s logistics costs at around 8 per cent of GDP, challenging the earlier perception that they accounted for 13-14 per cent.

India has also improved its position in the Logistics Performance Index (LPI), moving from 46th in 2018 to 30th.

Infrastructure connectivity remains central to improving logistics efficiency, with better links needed between manufacturing hubs, consumption centres and last-mile destinations.
The government launched PM Gati Shakti in 2021 as a digital platform to coordinate infrastructure planning across ministries.

The platform helps identify gaps in connectivity, locate underserved areas and anticipate implementation hurdles, including forest areas and restricted zones, before projects reach the execution stage.
This enables authorities to plan clearances in advance and reduce delays during implementation, the official said.
The pace of road construction has increased from around 5-6 km a day to more than 15 km a day on average, according to the official.

It may be recalled that in June, the Court held a Kerala resident, Krishnankutty, guilty of contempt for violating an undertaking that the elephant would not be subjected to commercial exploitation pending the adjudication of the present dispute.
Subsequently, it directed the State to take over the custody of Raman and house it in an appropriate rescue or rehabilitation centre.
Today, the matter came up before a bench comprising Justice Dipankar Datta and Justice Sheel Nagu.
When Justice Datta asked about the whereabouts of the elephant, the caretaker informed that it was with him because the elephant was in a state of musth and couldn't be shifted.
The State's counsel also supported this argument, but the petitioner's counsel opposed it, stating that whenever there is an order to shift the elephant, the state of musth is "induced artificially."
This compelled Justice Datta to remark: "We will not allow you[the caretaker] to touch it[the elephant]".
The caretaker submitted that the elephant has been treated with love and care.
But Justice Datta responded that the musth issue had happened only for a few months and questioned what steps have been taken subsequent to the Court's order.
He also told the caretaker: "Love, care and for the purpose of earning money by defying the Supreme Court's restraint orders.
We quite understand what love and affection is.
We are not going to hear you."

stories.title: Telangana CM Revanth to review El Nino impact, drought conditions on October 12
stories.summary: The action plan prepared by Telangana Cabinet sub-committee on drought mitigation, along with relief measures likely to be examined
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy will hold a special meeting with Ministers on October 12 to review the impact of El Nino and the prevailing rainfall deficit in Telangana, with a focus on relief measures for farmers and steps to address emerging water and power requirements.

The meeting is expected to take stock of conditions in areas that have received insufficient rainfall, the difficulties faced by farmers and the immediate interventions required to mitigate the impact of the dry spell.
Agriculture, irrigation, drinking water supply and the rising demand for electricity will be among the key issues on the agenda.
The move comes after an extensive discussion on the rainfall deficit at the recent State Cabinet meeting.
Telangana has recorded 17% less rainfall than normal, with drought-like conditions prevailing in nearly 235 mandals, according to official estimates cited by the government.
The State government has already adopted a resolution in the Legislative Assembly urging the Centre to declare drought-affected mandals and extend adequate financial assistance.
It has also sought a special package of Rs.
20,000 crore to help the State tackle the impact of the deficient rainfall.

The meeting on Tuesday is likely to examine the action plan prepared by the Cabinet sub-committee on drought mitigation, along with relief measures that need to be taken up in rainfall-deficient areas.
Suggestions emerging from political parties, consultations with farmers’ organisations and inputs from experts in various sectors are also expected to figure in the discussions.
